title: Fin Box Rib Web — Dent Blending and Local Reinforcement

issue.reason: Original issue of the dent blending and local reinforcement repair for the fin box rib web.

abstract: Repair of a dented fin box rib web caused by handling during internal access, with a blend depth allowance measured down from the nominal web thickness and an optional reinforcement disc.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the buckling capability of a fin box rib web after a handling dent, and gives the blend depth that may be taken out of the web.
sections.damage_assessment: Almost every dent in this position comes from a foot or from a dropped tool during internal access, so check whether the reporting technician entered the fin box before the damage was found. Measure the dent depth with the dial gauge on the straight edge and record the depth, the diameter and the distance to the nearest stiffener land. The blend allowance is taken down from the nominal web thickness of 4.0 mm and the remaining thickness after blending must not be less than 3.4 mm at any point. A dent that reaches a stiffener land or a fastener row, or that has a sharp crease at its base, is outside the scope of this repair.
sections.repair_procedure: Support the rib with the internal cradle before any work starts and do not stand on the web at any time during the repair. Clean the dented area on both faces and remove the protective treatment locally. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the dent base over its full diameter and confirm that no crease crack is present. Blend the raised material on the convex face with a fine abrasive to a smooth transition, taking not more than the depth given for the web standard on repair drawing RD-55-30-11-907. Do a second dye penetrant inspection after blending. Where the dent depth is more than half the limit, install the local reinforcement disc from the drawing on the concave face, bonded and secured with screws AES932279K1 into anchor nuts EN675891-15 at the pattern shown. Apply the chemical conversion coating, the primer and the topcoat of ATA 51-20 to the whole repaired area on both faces. Record the repair position, the dent depth and the remaining web thickness on the aircraft structural record sheet. Remove the internal cradle only after the protective treatment has cured.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a general visual inspection of the repaired web at every fin box internal inspection and an ultrasonic thickness measurement of the blended region at every second one. Not more than two repaired positions per rib and not more than four per fin box. Report the repair to Aeralis with the measured remaining thickness.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Dents up to 1.2 mm deep and 60 mm in diameter, with the remaining web thickness after blending not less than 3.4 mm. No dent may reach a stiffener land, a fastener row, or show a crease at its base.

repair_drawings.title: Dent blending limits and reinforcement disc, fin box rib web

type_data.fastener_pattern: Twelve screws on a 90 mm pitch circle around the reinforcement disc, where a disc is required
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit where the remaining thickness after blending is not less than 3.4 mm.

title: Fin Box Rib Web — Dent Blending and Local Reinforcement

issue.reason: Depth limits split by web standard and a repaired rib declared ineligible for the pocketed set until the pocketed-web blending variant is published.

abstract: Repair of a dented fin box rib web caused by handling during internal access, with different depth limits for the solid and the pocketed web standards.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the buckling capability of a fin box rib web after a handling dent, and gives the depth limits that apply to each web standard.
sections.damage_assessment: Almost every dent in this position comes from a foot or from a dropped tool during internal access, so check whether the reporting technician entered the fin box before the damage was found. Establish the web standard first by measuring the web thickness at the reference position: the solid web is 4.0 mm and the pocketed web is 2.6 mm outside the stiffener lands, and the depth limits differ accordingly. Measure the dent depth with the dial gauge on the straight edge and record the depth, the diameter and the distance to the nearest stiffener land. A dent that reaches a stiffener land or a fastener row, or that has a sharp crease at its base, is outside the scope of this repair on either web standard.
sections.repair_procedure: Support the rib with the internal cradle before any work starts and do not stand on the web at any time during the repair. Clean the dented area on both faces and remove the protective treatment locally. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the dent base over its full diameter and confirm that no crease crack is present. Blend the raised material on the convex face with a fine abrasive to a smooth transition, taking not more than the depth given for the web standard on repair drawing RD-55-30-11-907. Do a second dye penetrant inspection after blending. Where the dent depth is more than half the limit, install the local reinforcement disc from the drawing on the concave face, bonded and secured with screws AES932279K1 into anchor nuts EN675891-15 at the pattern shown. Apply the chemical conversion coating, the primer and the topcoat of ATA 51-20 to the whole repaired area on both faces. Record the repair position, the dent depth and the remaining web thickness on the aircraft structural record sheet. Remove the internal cradle only after the protective treatment has cured.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a general visual inspection of the repaired web at every fin box internal inspection and an ultrasonic thickness measurement of the blended region at every second one. A pocketed web that carries this repair may not be blended a second time at the same position. A rib that carries a blend at or within 25 mm of a pocket boundary position is outside the effectivity of Service Bulletin CRN-55-1004 and may not be exchanged for a pocketed item: the blend was taken against the solid web thickness and the same material removal on a pocketed rib leaves the web below the static minimum. A pocketed-web form of this blending scheme is being prepared by the repair office and will be issued as a separate arrangement on this repair. Not more than two repaired positions per rib and not more than four per fin box. Report the repair to Aeralis with the web standard and the measured remaining thickness.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: On the solid web, dents up to 1.2 mm deep and 60 mm in diameter. On the pocketed web, dents up to 0.6 mm deep and 40 mm in diameter. No dent may reach a stiffener land, a fastener row, or show a crease at its base.

repair_drawings.title: Dent blending limits and reinforcement disc, fin box rib web

type_data.fastener_pattern: Twelve screws on a 90 mm pitch circle around the reinforcement disc, where a disc is required
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit. A pocketed web position that carries this repair may not be blended a second time.
